passage: Nilesh had been late to the eight o'clock lecture nine times in a month, and Binita, the hostel warden, asked him to stop by her office. Instead of scolding, she asked, 'Why are you late?' 'I wake up late.' 'Why?' 'I sleep late.' 'Why?' He shrugged. 'I scroll on my phone in bed until two.' 'And why do you scroll?' 'I just keep doing it. It's a habit.' Nilesh looked at the floor. He didn't need a louder alarm; he needed the phone out of reach. That night he put the charger on a shelf in the corridor, beyond the reach of his bed. By Friday he was in his seat at ten to eight.

passage:
Dear Jatin bhai,
You asked how I stopped getting marked late at the hostel gate every morning. The warden had warned me twice, and I was sure I just needed a louder alarm.
Then I tried asking why, properly. Why am I late? Because I can't get up at the alarm. Why? Because I'm exhausted. Why? Because I sleep at two. Why? Because I'm on my phone in bed till then. Why? Because I scroll every night without deciding to. It's a habit.
So a louder alarm was never the answer. The phone in bed was.
Now I charge my phone on the study table across the room, and I don't bring it to bed. The first three nights were hard. By the second week I was asleep by midnight.
I've been on time for eleven days straight.
Irfan

qa.q: Where does Irfan now charge the phone?
qa.a: On the study table across the room.

qa.q: How did Irfan feel during the first three nights?
qa.a: Irfan found them hard, probably restless and tempted to reach for the phone, before the new habit settled.

qa.q: Why was moving the phone better than getting a louder alarm?
qa.a: It fixed the root cause, late-night scrolling, instead of the symptom, so Irfan actually slept enough to wake on time.

qa.q: How might the warden see Irfan's eleven days on time?
qa.a: The warden may be relieved and pleased that the warnings led to a real change, not just excuses.

grounding: It shows a hostel student tracing lateness to poor sleep, late phone use and a scrolling habit, and acting on the root by charging the phone outside the bed.

passage:
Sharmila, you want to know how your cousin Abhinav became the first one at breakfast? It's a bit embarrassing, but okay.
Second semester, I was late for the 8 a.m. lecture almost every day. My attendance was falling. I kept blaming the hostel alarm, the noisy corridor, everything.
Then one night I sat down and asked myself why five times. Late, because I oversleep. Oversleep, because I'm tired. Tired, because I sleep at 2.30. Sleep late, because I'm on my phone. On my phone, because I scroll without noticing, every night, out of habit.
The alarm was never the problem. The phone was.
So I did one simple thing. The charger went into the corridor socket outside our room, and the phone stayed there all night. My roommate thought I was mad.
Three weeks now. Asleep by twelve. Not a single late mark.

qa.q: Where did Abhinav put the charger?
qa.a: Into the corridor socket outside the room.

qa.q: How did Abhinav feel about telling this story?
qa.a: Abhinav felt a bit embarrassed, admitting that blaming the alarm and the corridor had hidden the real reason.

qa.q: What else could Abhinav do if the scrolling moves to the laptop?
qa.a: Abhinav could set a fixed time to shut the laptop too, since the root cause is the late-night habit, not one device.

qa.q: How might the roommate see Abhinav's new habit?
qa.a: The roommate first thinks Abhinav is mad, but may later notice the change and even feel encouraged to try it.
